correctness.rationale: Direct monomial integration yields alpha_n=2a sqrt((n+1)/(n+2)) and beta_n=b/sqrt(n+1). Subtracting V*V and VV* yields d_0=2|a|^2+|b|^2, d_n=8|a|^2/[n(n+2)]-|b|^2/[n(n+1)] for n>=1, t_0=a conj(b), t_n=-2a conj(b)/[(n+2)sqrt(n+1)] for n>=1. Sum of |d_n| and |t_n| is finite; exact partial trace telescoping gives 8|a|^2. Three-band singular-value inequality gives upper O(n^-3/2) (O(n^-2) for ab=0); sparse compression onto 3k,3k+1 supplies lower Ω(n^-3/2) when ab≠0, while pure cases are diagonal with nonzero n^-2 tails. Disjoint 4k,4k+1 pair quadratic forms prove infinite signed inertia in the mixed case. The independently constructed finite matrix checker passed 21010 assertions; finite tests do not establish the infinite conclusions.

value.rationale: Completes the quantitative operator-ideal refinement of the focal 2026 essential-normality result throughout the entire bounded-symbol class: the mere presence of a nonzero linear coefficient changes the sharp singular-value order and critical quasi-Schatten exponent from 2 to 3/2 (p from 1/2 to 2/3), while the trace depends only on the quadratic coefficient. The infinite two-sided signed inertia in the mixed regime is an additional spectral distinction. These natural and exact invariants measure how far essentially normal Volterra operators are from actual normality beyond a qualitative compactness statement.
